texts.preamble: Parul vs Vipin Kumar on 20 January, 2026
texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) for compensation relates to grievous injury suffered by the claimant Parul in a road accident that took place on 01.04.2018 at about 07:50 PM, Near Gate No. 2, Nagal Dewat Gaon, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.143/18 was registered at PS Vasant Kunj South. 2. The offending vehicle involved in this case is a three wheeler bearing registration No. DL-1LL-1986, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 Vipin Kumar, registered in the name of respondent no. 2 Jitender Kumar, subsequently purchased by respondent no. 3 Vijay and thereafter, purchased by respondent no. 4 Dharmender. Case of the claimant 3. It is the case of the claimant that on 01.04.2018, she along with her mother Smt. Poonam and her brother Kunal were going on scooty No. DL-3SCD-7119 from Nangal Devat Red light to her residence at Vasant Kunj Enclave, Delhi which was being driven by her. When they reached at Gate No. 2, Nangal Devat Village, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1LL-1986, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, came from Vasant Kunj Enclave side in a wrong direction and hit their scooty from the front due to which they fell down on the road and sustained injuries. It is further stated that the claimant was taken to Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi where her MLC was prepared by the doctors. Case of respondent no. 2 4. Respondent no. 2/owner filed his reply to the DAR wherein it is stated that he has sold the alleged offending vehicle to respondent no. 3 Vijay on 23.09.2023 against a total sale consideration of Rs.59,000/- and the said fact was reduced in writing between them in the presence of witnesses. It is further stated that Sh. Vijay had also put his signatures on delivery receipt and he had also given Form 35 duly signed by him to Sh. Vijay for the purpose of transfer of the aforesaid vehicle. It is further stated that the the accident took place on account of negligent driving of Poonam who was driving her scooty without having valid driving license. It is further stated that Poonam was driving her scooty with two pillion riders which is clear violation of traffic rules and norms. Case of respondent no. 4 5. Respondent no. 4 filed his reply to the DAR wherein it is stated that he is not entitled to pay any compensation to the claimant as he has no concern with the alleged accident. It is further stated that the rider of scooty was driving her scooty with pillion riders and was not holding any valid and effective driving license at the time of accident. It is further stated that the accident took place due to sole and absolute negligence on the part of rider of the scooty. 6. Vide order dated 14.11.2022, respondents no. 1 and 2 were proceeded against ex-parte. 7. It is pertinent to mention that vide order dated 08.03.2019, three connected DARs bearing DAR Nos. 635/18, 636/18 & 641/18 arising out of the same accident were consolidated for the purpose of Parul vs Vipin Kumar on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38180140/ 2 trial and DAR No. 635/18 was directed to be treated as the lead case for recording of evidence. Issues 8. On 08.03.2019, the following consolidated issues were framed by this Tribunal :- 1. Whether Kunal (minor injured in D-635/18), Smt. Poonam (injured in D-636/18) and Parul (minor injured in D-641/18) sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 02.04.2018 at about 07:50 PM, Road Near Gate No. 2, Nagal Dewat Gaon, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-1LL-1986 being driven by respondent no. 1, registered in the name of respondent no. 2, alleged to have been sold by respondent no. 2 to respondent no. 3 and then respondent no. 3 to respondent no. 4 ? OPP. 2. OPP. 3. Relief. Claimant's evidence 9. In support of her claim, the claimant examined herself as PW2. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW2/A and relied upon the following documents :- (i). Ex. PW2/1 (OSR) is the copy of her Aadhaar card. (ii). Ex.PW2/2 (OSR) is the copy of her PAN card. (iii). Ex. PW2/3 is her MLC. (iv). Ex. PW2/4 (colly) are her treatment record. (v). Ex. PW2/5 (colly) are her medical bills. (vi). Ex. PW1/5 is the DAR filed by the IO. Ex. PW2/6 (colly) are the photographs showing her injuries. 10. The claimant also examined her mother Smt. Poonam, who is also injured in the connected matter as PW1. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A and relied upon the following documents :- Parul vs Vipin Kumar on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38180140/ 3 (i). Ex. PW1/1 is the copy of Aadhaar card of her son. Ex. PW1/12 (colly) are the photographs showing her injuries. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2W1/A and relied upon copies of sale letter, delivery receipts and NOC as Mark R2W1/1 (colly). 13. Respondent no. 2 examined Sh. Ram Chander who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2W3/A and relied upon original delivery receipts as Ex.R2W1/1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. DW3/1A and relied upon the copy of his Aadhaar card as Ex.DW3/1 (OSR) and the policy of insurance as Ex. DW3/2 (OSR). Findings 15. PW2 in her affidavit Ex. PW2/A has tendered on record her treatment record as Ex. PW2/4 (colly), as per which the claimant was admitted in Indian Spinal Injuries Centre on 01.04.2018 and was discharged on 03.04.2018 where she was diagnosed with open fracture right middle phalanx with deep laceration on volar and dorsal aspect of middle finger with undisplaced fracture right distal end radius and had undergone operative procedure.
texts.arguments: He argued that Smt. Poonam was not holding a valid driving license and was riding the two wheeler with two pillion riders. He also argued that the three wheeler was not coming from the wrong side. He submitted that on the road where the accident took place, there was two-way traffic and it was not one-way traffic road. 20. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Saraswati Palariya and Ors. Vs New India Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors., 2019 ACJ 42 has held that driving without a driving license may expose the person to other liabilities but no inference of contributory negligence can be drawn on that basis. 21. In Mohammed Siddique & Anr. Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. AIR 2020 SUPREME COURT 520, it has been held as follows: "13. But the above reason, in our view, is flawed. At the most it would Parul vs Vipin Kumar on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38180140/ 5 make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law. Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two- wheeled motor cycle, not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle. Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law. Therefore, an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no.1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310. 24. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced." 25. Chargesheet was also filed against the respondent no.1/driver of the vehicle. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently. It has been further observed that even when the accused was acquitted in the criminal case, the same will have no effect on the assessment of liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal. Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. 27. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:- Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 30. 34. During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for claimant has conceded that the minimum wages of a matriculate may be granted since the claimant was matriculate on the date of accident. Accordingly, the claimant should be awarded minimum wages of a matriculate as per rates prevalent in Delhi, which was Rs. 16,858/- per month at the time of accident. 35. Keeping in view the nature of injuries and duration of her treatment, this Tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate her for loss of earning equivalent to a period of three months. Therefore, under this head, she is being awarded an amount of Rs.50,574/- (Rs.16,858/- X 3 months). The liability to pay compensation is of the registered owner and in this context, reliance is placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar & Ors., 2018 AIR (SC) 983, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with a case of multiple transfers of an uninsured vehicle has allowed an appeal filed by a purchaser of the offending vehicle and has [LEAKAGE_MASK] the judgment of the Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court holding him liable to pay compensation, which in turn set-aside the judgment/award passed by a Claims Tribunal holding the registered owner of offending vehicle, along with driver thereof, to be liable for making payment of an award passed in the said case. The following was held in this case :- "12. In Dr T V Jose, this Court observed that there can be transfer of title by payment of Parul vs Vipin Kumar on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38180140/ 12 consideration and delivery of the car. But for the purposes of the Act, the person whose name is reflected in the records of the registering authority is the owner. The owner within the meaning of Section 2(30) is liable to compensate. The mandate of the law must be fulfilled. In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs." 56. The above propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Naveen Kumar (supra) have even been followed and reiterated subsequently by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prakash Chand Daga Vs. Saveta Sharma & Ors., 2018 LawSuit (SC) 176, wherein the findings of the Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana holding a registered owner to be liable in place of purchaser and possessor thereof, was upheld. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held the following :- "9. The law is thus well settled and can be summarised:- Merely because the vehicle was transferred does not mean that such registered owner stands absolved of his liability to a third person.
